summary: Embed upload checksum scan triggers ephemeral-proxy CPU spike and downstream 5xx wave
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably AtlasSearch Inc.) reported elevated 502/503/504 rates beginning ~2026-03-14T11:18Z on embedding upload and small generation routes. Errors surface primarily at api-gateway; traces show upstream connection resets and runtime process exits shortly after.

Impact:
- Multiple tenants in prod-us-east observed a 5xx increase from baseline ~0.2% -> 7% for ~20 minutes.
- Embedded file uploads (multipart) and small embed generation routes returned 502/504; streaming routes saw intermittent resets.
- Customer-facing degradation for dedicated tenants (AtlasSearch, MeridianAI).

Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated capacity pool and shared ephemeral proxies)
- Affected path: /v1/embeddings/bulk, /v1/generate (short payloads), streaming endpoints

Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload a large multipart embedding file (~1.2GB, 16 parts) via the bulk-embed API from a dedicated tenant.
2) Observe background checksum validator job start (storage service log shows checkpointing).
3) Within 2-5 minutes, ephemeral-proxy CPU spikes to 90-100%, accept queue grows, and api-gateway begins returning 502/504.
4) Upstream serving-runtime processes report watch-dog timeouts and occasional SIGTERM restarts.

Logs / evidence:
- api-gateway logs (sample): "upstream reset before response: connection reset by peer" at 2026-03-14T11:22:11Z.
- ephemeral-proxy metrics: cpu_user jumped from 12% -> 96%, accept_queue length +420 between 11:20-11:25Z.
- storage service logs: "checksum-scan: background validation started for multipart manifest id=mnf-78f2" at 11:19:58Z.
- serving-runtime stderr: "Watchdog: no-progress timeout, killing worker pid=4127" followed by OOM-killer messages in dmesg.
- Tracing link: https://traces.redwood.com/trace/xyz-embed-246801

Current workaround provided to customer:
- Ask customers to split large embedding uploads into time-separated batches and to enable client-side retry jitter.
- Temporarily paused non-critical background checksum scans in prod-us-east (manual action by storage ops).
investigation_notes:
Timeline & hypotheses:
- 11:18Z: AtlasSearch bulk-embed upload arrives. Storage starts multipart commit and triggers checksum validation.
- 11:20Z: Storage I/O increases (nvme iowait >80%), ephemeral-proxy CPU climbs; proxies are performing synchronous write/metadata operations on behalf of uploads.
- 11:22Z: Accept queue backlog causes api-gateway backpressure; gateway hedged retries amplify load and trigger runtime preemption.
- 11:24Z: Some serving-runtime pods hit memory pressure and the kernel OOM reclaims worker processes, causing 502/504.

Hypothesis validated by correlating storage IO spikes, proxy CPU, and runtime OOMs. Not a pure kernel bug or model kernel fallback: kernel selection logs show normal operation. Root cause appears to be combined: heavy multipart upload + synchronous checksum scan holding proxy threads while the I/O path causes CPU+io saturation, amplifying accept-queue and hedged retries.

Partial findings & artifacts:
- Sysstat (iostat) from node n-edge-17 shows nvme_avg_quque > 300ms during the window.
- Ephemeral-proxy traces show long-tail syscall blocks on fsync during checksum stage.
- No config change or deployment at 11:15; reproducible with a synthetic large multipart upload in perf cluster (staging) when background checksum enabled.

Next investigation steps:
- Reproduce in dedicated staging with storage perf flags and collect flamegraphs for ephemeral-proxy.
- Confirm whether multipart checksum runs on sync path; if so, move to async background worker.
- Audit rate limits and hedged-retry policy that may amplify backpressure.

Stakeholders looped: support (#support), sres (#sre-frontend), storage eng (#storage).

resolution:
(work in progress) Immediate mitigations applied: paused background checksum scans in prod-us-east and asked tenants to stagger large embed uploads. Temporary limit applied to concurrent multipart commits.
Planned fix: storage change to move checksum validation off the synchronous commit path into an async validator (PR #102) + limit concurrent checksum workers and add IO-throttling on background validation.
Operational follow-ups:
- Add alert for storage iowait > 50% that triggers auto-throttle of background validators.
- Update runbook with steps to pause checksum workers and recommended tenant ingestion best practices.
- Postmortem to be produced after rollback windows and canary validation (linked to INT-442).
notes_for_postmortem: Items to cover in postmortem: why checksum validation was synchronous; why hedged retry/backpressure amplified failure; capacity planning for embedding ingestion; customer communication timeline and SLA impact calculation.
